text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Employees of state-run Posta Romana RA postal authority started a series of strikes across the country on Monday to demand bonuses for the winter holidays.
- New transport minister Traian Basescu plans to raise train fares.
- The National association for investors' protection calls for a suspension of the National shareholders' register on grounds it allegedly affects the shareholders' interests.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania's annual exports should amount to some $15 billion, state secretary Mihai Berinde is quoted as saying.
- Bucharest Court of Appeal rejected a demand by private oil company to dissolve the state-run National Oil Company.
- Unprofitable companies will be declared bankrupt and sold to Romanian and foreign investors, reform minister Ulm Spineanu said.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The State Ownership Fund should be subordinated to the government and parliament, Spineanu said.
- Romanians spend their savings buying Christhmas presents although they see themselves as poor, the paper says.
- Havaline Agriculture of Canada wants to invest in Romania's farming sector, the paper says.
ZIUA
- Trade unions in the mining sector plan to open a bank to finance investments in the sector.
- Prices of tractors made by tractor factroy in Brasov are to rise by 40 percent.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- The National Peasant Party (PNT-CD), backbone of the Democratic Convention (CDR) which won general elections last month, will hold the chairmanship of the parliament commission controlling the Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI).

- Communists control all leading structures in Moldova now after Petru Lucinschi won the presidential elections last month, says Iurie Rosca, head of the Christian Democratic Popular Front, in an interview.
- The newspaper publishes a full page of documents produced by army leaders during the December 1989 revolution.
ADEVARUL

- Miron Cosma, the miners' union leader who led rampages to Bucharest in 1990 and toppled the reformist government of former Prime Minister Petre Roman a year later, said that "the moral authors, some of whom are still in power" must be judged too for those rampages.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The newspaper publishes reactions to the government's decision to appoint film director Stere Gulea as interim chairman of the state television.

- The three coalition members -- CDR, the Social Democratic Union (USD) and the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) -- distributed the 65 posts of state secretaries with the CDR taking 40, USD 17 and UDMR 8.
ZIUA
- The newspaper publishes a message adressed by ex-King Michael to the Romanian people to mark seven years since the December 1989 revolution.
LIBERTATEA
- The newspaper presents the five advisers of President Emil Constantinescu.
- Romanians will be allowed to enter the park of the presidential palace of Cotroceni at Christmas.
AZI
- Defence Minister Victor Babiuc said his priorities were to draw up Romania's defence strategy and a "white book" on national security as well as changing the law on the Supreme Defence Council.
CRONICA ROMANA
- The UDMR obtained three posts of county prefects, five of deputy prefects and six of general managers. ($=3,792 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
